## Key Findings

### How Ontologies Improve Semantic Search with Knowledge Graphs

Semantic search is an advanced technology for knowledge discovery that employs a set of semantic technology techniques for retrieving knowledge from richly structured data sources. By using the knowledge graph model, it enables AI systems to understand the meaning of concepts and the relationships between them, which leads to optimizing the accuracy of the results and making them highly contextual and personalized.

### The Role of Ontologies

What makes a knowledge graph a semantic knowledge graph is the semantic (data) model, or ontology, that is part of it. An ontology enriches data within a knowledge graph with context and meaning that humans and computers can interpret.(no content)An ontology is a formal, explicit specification of a shared conceptualization of a domain. Rather than representing individual facts, an ontology defines the types of entities, relationships, constraints, and rules that describe how knowledge in a domain is structured. It serves as a semantic blueprint that ensures consistency, clarity, and shared understanding.

### Knowledge Graph Benefits for Search

Knowledge graphs may make use of ontologies as a schema layer. By doing this, they allow logical inference for retrieving implicit knowledge rather than only allowing queries requesting explicit knowledge.(no content)In the last several decades, when people consider building a knowledge-related solution, they tend to look into two distinct directions based on whether data is structured or unstructured. Accordingly, there is the so-called structured search using a query language over a database or semantic search using inferencing and reasoning over the meaning of data, mostly text. With the rise of Large Language Models (LLM), there is a new and promising way to bring the two into ONE, i.e., to store both structure and meaning in a knowledge graph.

### Performance Improvements

In recent benchmark studies conducted by data.world, integrating an ontology-backed knowledge graph with a large language model (LLM) yielded dramatic improvements in performance. In a controlled test of 43 enterprise-grade questions and across complex schemas, adding ontology-based query validation and repair boosted LLM accuracy by more than 4.2 times.

### Restaurant Industry Application

One use case involves a complex ordering experience in a quick-service restaurant serving thousands of customizable product variants. The solution combined semantic Knowledge Graph with the Agent Framework to intelligently identify products, properties, or relationships.

### RAG and Knowledge Graphs

Research shows that integrating textual chunks directly into the graph structure, beyond traditional entity and relation-only Knowledge Graphs, improves retrieval accuracy and generation quality by enriching context and enabling deeper reasoning. Additionally, ontologies extracted from static relational databases yield performance comparable to those derived from text corpora, while being far more cost-efficient and easier to maintain.

## FoodOn: Food Ontology Overview

FoodOn is an ontology – a controlled vocabulary which can be used by both people and computers – to name all parts of animals, plants, and fungi which can bear a food role for humans and domesticated animals, as well as derived food products and the processes used to make them.

### Core Purpose and Structure

Well defined, hierarchical vocabulary, connected with logical relationships—in other words, an ontology—is urgently needed to help tackle data harmonization problems that span the domains of food security, safety, quality, production, distribution, and consumer health and convenience.(no content)The "food material" hierarchy contains FoodOn's main "food product" polyhierarchy of over 9,600 food products, as well as upper-level international, European and American food categorization schemas which will ultimately be mapped to FoodOn product type categories.

### OBO Foundry Integration

FoodOn belongs to the open source OBO Foundry consortium of interoperable life science oriented ontologies and consequently supports FAIR data annotation and sharing objectives across a wide variety of academic research, government and commercial sectors.(no content)FoodOn reuses terms from OBO Foundry ontologies such as environmental terms from ENVO, agriculture terms from AGRO, plant and animal anatomy terms from UBERON and PO, organisms from NCBITaxon. Conversely, FoodOn terms are reused in a growing list of ontologies such as ENVO, CDNO, ONE, ONS, FIDEO, FOBI, ECTO, and DOID.

### Recent Developments (2024-2025)

Join us at the sixth annual Integrated Food Ontology Workshop as part of FOIS 2025 September 8-12 in Catania Italy (exact date to be defined). Find out the latest developments since last year, and contribute to the evolution of food and recipe ontology!(no content)Since its creation in 2016, the FoodOn food ontology has become an interconnected partner in various academic and government projects that span agricultural and public health domains. This paper examines recent data interoperability capabilities arising from food-related ontologies belonging to, or compatible with, the encyclopedic Open Biological and Biomedical Ontology Foundry (OBO) ontology platform.

### Applications with Large Language Models (2025)

FoodSEM is a fine-tuned open-source LLM for food NEL. Through an instruction-response (IR) scenario, FoodSEM is able to link food-related entity mentions in a text to entities from three food ontologies (FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and the Hansard taxonomy).(no content)The FoodSEM model achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to related models/systems, with F1 scores even reaching 98% on some ontologies and datasets.

### History and Origins

At its launch in 2018, FoodOn was based largely on LanguaL, a descriptive food indexing system that has 14 facets for describing food source plant and animal organisms, food preservation, cooking, packaging, consumer groups, labelling, etc.

### Key Resources

- **Website**: [foodon.org](https://foodon.org/)
- **GitHub**: [FoodOntology/foodon](https://github.com/FoodOntology/foodon)
- **Browser**: [EBI OLS FoodOn](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/foodon)

### FoodKG - A Major Knowledge Graph for Food Recommendations
The proliferation of recipes and other food information on the Web presents an opportunity for discovering and organizing diet-related knowledge into a knowledge graph. ### Pizza Restaurant Ontology Implementation
The design methodology begins with a systematic approach to Ontology Modeling using Protégé as the primary tool. The first step involved analyzing the Kaggle dataset of pizza restaurants to extract the main domain concepts such as Restaurant, Pizza, MenuItem, Ingredient, Location, and Cuisine Type.(no content)The RDF Generation stage transformed the Kaggle dataset into RDF triples guided by the ontology. Each row of the dataset was parsed and converted into entities and relationships represented in Turtle syntax, ensuring global uniqueness through URI assignment. For instance, a restaurant instance in the dataset was mapped to the Restaurant class, linked to its location, pizzas, and ingredients through defined object properties.

### Knowledge Graph Embedding for Recommendations
Incorporating knowledge graphs as side information to recommender systems by knowledge graph embedding techniques has attracted considerable interest, because the rich information contained in the knowledge graph can effectively solve problems like sparse interaction data and cold-start problems.(no content)Chang et al. (2019) divided existing KG-based recommendation methods into two major categories: ontology-based methods and LOD-based methods (open linked data).

RecKG is a standardized knowledge graph for recommender systems that ensures the consistent representation of entities across different datasets, accommodating diverse attribute types for effective data integration. Introducing a knowledge graph (KG) into recommender systems as side information has attracted great interest since a KG can provide extra information and can be used to suggest potential relations among items. ## Key Differences: Semantic Search with Ontology vs. Keyword Search

### Keyword Search Limitations

### Semantic Search Advantages

Unlike traditional keyword search, it can understand synonyms, interpret conversational queries, and recognize that "best running shoes" relates to athletic footwear, sneakers, and jogging gear.

### Restaurant Discovery Examples
Modern keyword search is already far more semantic than its early predecessors. When a user types "best Italian restaurant nearby," the system interprets intent, location, and preference — not just string matches.(no content)For example, the user's location helps it give you geographically spot-on results (a search for "best Italian restaurant" means something different for a user in Rome than in New York).(no content)Voice search: The user asks, "Where's the best Italian restaurant near me?" semantic search leverages location data and contextual information to provide results specific to their query.

### Role of Ontologies
Ontology based semantic search will lead to new generation of search based on the meaning of keyword rather than keyword and helps in finding correct information on the web. ### Challenges with Ontology-Based Approaches

While you can build highly robust solutions for one subject, it may fail completely for a different subject where a different area of expertise is needed.

Most large discovery platforms already operate as hybrids, blending lexical, semantic, and behavioral signals behind the scenes. Rather than disappearing, keywords are increasingly becoming infrastructure — working "under the hood" even when users interact through natural language interfaces.(no content)The future of search is moving heavily towards semantic and vector-based approaches which place their emphasis on meaning, context, and user satisfaction. # FoodKG Construction Methodology & Ontology

## Construction Methodology

FoodKG integrates multiple data sources into a unified knowledge graph. The process follows these steps:

1. **Data Acquisition**: Gather recipe data, nutrient information, and food knowledge from various sources
2. **Data Preparation**: Use preprocessing scripts to combine manually-acquired and automatically-downloaded data
3. **Graph Generation**: Apply recipe handlers to create RDF triples from prepared datasets
4. **Validation**: Generate statistics to verify result quality

## Data Sources & Ontologies

**Recipe Data**: "Recipes can be derived from a multitude of sources, such as books, websites, and structured datasets," sourced from the Im2Recipe project collection.

**Nutrient Data**: USDA nutrient information integrated via Semantic Data Dictionaries, with mappings to external ontologies including FoodOn and Units Ontology.

**Food Knowledge**: "The ontology provides detailed information about the origin and preparation of foods" through FoodOn incorporation.

## Graph Structure

The final output comprises three serialized RDF files:
- **usda-links.trig** (~4.1 million triples)
- **foodon-links.trig** (~30 thousand triples)  
- **foodkg-core.trig** (~63 million triples)

These files enable loading into graph databases like BlazeGraph for natural language query execution.

# 레스토랑/푸드 서비스 도메인 온톨로지 연구 보고서

## 1. 기존 레스토랑 온톨로지 표준

### 1.1 Schema.org Restaurant 및 FoodEstablishment

[Schema.org](https://schema.org/)는 구글, 마이크로소프트, 야후, Yandex가 공동으로 만든 구조화된 데이터 표준으로, 레스토랑 도메인에 대해 다음과 같은 계층 구조를 제공합니다:

**타입 계층 구조:**
```
Thing → Organization → LocalBusiness → FoodEstablishment → Restaurant
```

**[FoodEstablishment](https://schema.org/FoodEstablishment) 하위 타입:**
- Bakery (베이커리)
- BarOrPub (바/펍)
- Brewery (양조장)
- CafeOrCoffeeShop (카페)
- Distillery (증류소)
- FastFoodRestaurant (패스트푸드)
- IceCreamShop (아이스크림 가게)
- Restaurant (레스토랑)
- Winery (와이너리)

**핵심 속성들:**

| 속성 | 설명 | Findining 적용 가능성 |
|------|------|---------------------|
| `servesCuisine` | 요리 종류 (한식, 중식, 일식 등) | 음식 카테고리 분류에 직접 활용 |
| `hasMenu` | 메뉴 정보 (URL, 텍스트, 구조화 데이터) | 메뉴 기반 검색 |
| `acceptsReservations` | 예약 가능 여부 | 예약 필터링 |
| `priceRange` | 가격대 ("$", "$$", "$$$") | 가격 필터 |
| `aggregateRating` | 종합 평점 | 리뷰 기반 검색 |
| `openingHoursSpecification` | 영업시간 상세 | 영업시간 기반 검색 |
| `maximumAttendeeCapacity` | 최대 수용 인원 | 회식 인원 기반 검색 |

**Findining에의 적용 권장사항:**
Schema.org 속성을 확장하여 한국형 레스토랑 특성을 추가하면, SEO 최적화와 함께 표준화된 데이터 구조를 확보할 수 있습니다.

---

### 1.2 W3C Restaurant Ontology Community Group

[W3C Restaurant Ontology Community Group](https://www.w3.org/community/restonto/)은 레스토랑과 예약을 설명하기 위한 온톨로지를 개발했습니다 (2023년 4월 종료).

**지원 쿼리 유형:**
- "직장 근처 비즈니스 미팅용 아시안 레스토랑 찾기"
- "친구들과 식사 일정 잡고 캘린더에 추가하기"
- "신뢰할 수 있는 사람들의 좋은 리뷰가 있는 레스토랑 찾기"

이는 Findining이 목표로 하는 **상황 기반 검색**(회식, 데이트 등)과 직접적으로 연관됩니다.

---

## 2. 음식 온톨로지 표준 (FoodON, 음식 분류 체계)

### 2.1 FoodOn (Food Ontology)

[FoodOn](https://foodon.org/)은 OBO Foundry 컨소시엄에 속한 오픈소스 음식 온톨로지로, 2016년 출시 이후 학술 및 정부 프로젝트에서 널리 사용되고 있습니다.

**주요 특징:**
- **9,600개 이상의 식품 카테고리** 포함
- 동물, 식물, 균류의 식용 부위와 가공 식품, 제조 과정을 명명
- 국제/유럽/미국 식품 분류 스키마 통합
- [LanguaL](https://www.langual.org/) 기반 14가지 패싯(Facet) 체계:
  - 원산지 (동식물)
  - 보존 방법
  - 조리 방법
  - 포장 방식
  - 소비자 그룹

## 3. 온톨로지가 시맨틱 검색을 개선하는 방법

### 3.1 키워드 검색 vs 시맨틱 검색

| 특성 | 키워드 검색 | 온톨로지 기반 시맨틱 검색 |
|------|------------|------------------------|
| **매칭 방식** | 문자열 일치 | 의미 기반 연결 |
| **동의어 처리** | 불가능 | 자동 확장 |
| **계층 관계** | 미지원 | 상위/하위 개념 추론 |
| **문맥 이해** | 제한적 | 관계 기반 추론 |
| **예시** | "삼겹살" 검색 시 "삼겹살"만 반환 | "삼겹살" → "돼지고기", "한식", "구이류", "회식" 등 연관 개념 추론 |

### 3.2 온톨로지의 시맨틱 검색 개선 효과

[Ontotext 연구](https://www.ontotext.com/knowledgehub/fundamentals/what-is-semantic-search/)에 따르면:

1. **암묵적 지식 추론**: 명시적으로 저장되지 않은 관계도 추론 가능
2. **쿼리 확장**: "아시안" 검색 시 "중식", "일식", "태국식" 등 하위 개념 자동 포함
3. **다중 속성 결합**: "강남 + 25인 이상 + 회식 가능 + 족발" 같은 복합 쿼리 처리

[data.world 벤치마크](https://cyberhillpartners.com/enterprise-ai-ontologies-knowledge-graphs/)에서:
> "온톨로지 기반 지식 그래프를 LLM과 통합한 결과, **정확도가 4.2배 이상 향상**되었습니다."

### 3.3 RAG(Retrieval-Augmented Generation)와의 시너지

[최근 연구](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.05991v1)에 따르면:
- 텍스트 청크를 그래프 구조에 직접 통합하면 검색 정확도와 생성 품질이 향상
- 관계형 데이터베이스에서 추출한 온톨로지는 텍스트 코퍼스 기반과 비슷한 성능을 보이면서 **비용 효율적이고 유지보수가 용이**

### 5.4 시맨틱 검색 쿼리 처리 예시

**사용자 쿼리:** "족발집 25인 이상 회식 가능한 강남"

**온톨로지 기반 쿼리 확장:**

```
원본 쿼리 분석:
- 음식: 족발 → [족발, 보쌈, 야식류]
- 인원: 25인 이상 → groupSize >= 25
- 상황: 회식 → [회식, 단체모임, 회사행사]
- 지역: 강남 → [강남구, 강남역, 신논현, 역삼]

확장된 검색 조건:
1. cuisine IN (족발, 보쌈) OR tags CONTAINS (야식)
2. maxCapacity >= 25 OR hasPrivateRoom = true
3. suitableFor CONTAINS (회식) OR atmosphere IN (넓은공간, 단체환영)
4. location WITHIN 강남구 boundaries
5. hasGroupMenu = true (가산점)
```
